findings.title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-arg version
findings.body: Two `def self.downsize` methods are defined: the 4-argument `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145 and the 3-argument `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at line 149. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-arg form no longer exists. Any existing caller doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100)` now raises ArgumentError (or silently passes `100` as dimensions and `100` as opts). Keep one method, e.g. accept a dimensions string only, and update all callers.

findings.title: Removal of public helper `self.dimensions` and signature change of `optimize`
findings.body: `self.dimensions(width, height)` was removed and `self.optimize` changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`. These are public class methods that plugins/other code may call; the change breaks them without deprecation.

findings.title: Downsizing in place (from == to) can corrupt or truncate the tempfile
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` reads and writes the same path. ImageMagick's `convert` reading and writing the same file is unreliable, and the Ruby `Tempfile` object still has an open handle whose position/metadata is stale after the external process rewrites the file; `tempfile.size` and subsequent `Upload.create_for(... tempfile ...)` may see stale/incorrect data. Convert to a separate temp path and then replace/reopen the tempfile.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failures and can spin without progress
findings.body: The while loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times but never checks its boolean return value. If convert fails (missing binary, unsupported file), the file size never changes and the loop just burns 5 shell invocations per upload, then proceeds to create an upload that will be rejected for size. Check the return value and break/report an error on failure.

findings.title: Animated-GIF detection fails for tempfile paths
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated (gifsicle) code path via `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. A Rails uploaded `tempfile.path` normally ends in a random suffix (e.g. `RackMultipart2014...`), not `.gif`, so animated GIFs will be processed with `convert ...[0]`, flattening animation to the first frame even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on. Detect the type from the original filename/content type instead.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10.megabytes download limit replaces configurable setting
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was replaced by a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Sites configured to allow larger images (or intentionally smaller limits) no longer have their setting respected for API URL uploads; this also bypasses an administrator-configured resource limit. Use a setting (e.g. a new max upload size setting) instead of a magic constant.

findings.title: Client-side size validation hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Non-image attachments and sites with a different configured max size now get wrong client-side validation: files between the configured limit and 10MB are uploaded and then rejected by the server, and sites allowing >10MB attachments are blocked in the browser. The error message also reports a wrong limit to users.

findings.title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded, possibly wrong size limit
findings.body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 branch now shows a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. If the web server or site setting limit differs, the user is told an incorrect maximum size.

findings.title: No tests for the new auto-downsize path
findings.body: The new downsizing loop in `create_upload` (retry count, size threshold, non-image skip, failure handling) has no accompanying spec. Given it mutates the user's uploaded file in place, regressions would silently corrupt uploads.
